cite: Burke v. Brown, 10 Tex. Civ. App. 298
notes: Mechanic's-lien dispute over rental of tools used to physically move a house; no occupancy/lodging/letting issue. Selector false hit on 'erection'/'construction' language.

cite: Rentfrow v. Lancaster & Turner, 10 Tex. Civ. App. 321
notes: Wrongful-attachment/verdict-certainty case involving a landlord's crop-share lien and a guaranty dispute; 'landlord' here is a crop-share farm landlord, not a householder letting rooms/dwelling. No lodging or boarding issue.

cite: Finks v. Thompson, 11 Tex. Civ. App. 538
notes: Married woman's contract capacity/abandonment case; that she 'kept a boarding house in Waco' for two years is mentioned only as a background fact bearing on marital separation, not adjudicated for its own legal character. Passing mention only.

cite: Texas & Pacific Railway Co. v. Brown, 11 Tex. Civ. App. 503
notes: Attractive-nuisance/child-trespasser tort case in a railway switchyard; no occupancy or lodging issue. Selector false hit on 'permission or invitation' language.

cite: Missouri, Kansas & Texas Railway Co. v. Whitaker, 11 Tex. Civ. App. 668
notes: Fellow-servant doctrine case involving a roundhouse hostler and boiler washer; no occupancy/lodging issue whatsoever.

cite: Barrett v. Metcalfe, 12 Tex. Civ. App. 247
notes: Riparian irrigation-rights dispute under Texas water statutes; 'incident of ownership' language concerns water use, not letting of dwellings/rooms. No lodging issue.

cite: Wade v. Nunnelly, 19 Tex. Civ. App. 256
notes: City ordinance regulating street sale of produce (market/commerce use of streets), not lodging or boarding houses. Selector false hit on general municipal-police-power regulation language.

cite: Cross v. Freeman, 19 Tex. Civ. App. 428
notes: Executory land-sale contract with a contingent farm-rent clause pending title approval; ordinary agricultural landlord-tenant/estoppel dispute, no short-term room/dwelling letting or lodging-house regulation at issue.

cite: Manis v. Flood, 19 Tex. Civ. App. 591
notes: Statutory construction of who may distrain for farm rent (assignee of rent vs. assignee of reversion); a rented-land dispute, not householder/lodging letting.

cite: York v. Carlisle, 19 Tex. Civ. App. 269
notes: Tenant Pierce rented an entire house and lot from Mrs. York at $11/month for 8-10 months, but the sole issue litigated is the scope of the landlord's statutory lien on the tenant's horse; no discussion of the legal character or regulation of the letting itself. Ordinary full-house lease, not the room/lodging practice this corpus targets.

cite: Burton v. Dupree, 19 Tex. Civ. App. 275
notes: Lease void as against public policy because the house was knowingly let for prostitution; involves a city ordinance licensing houses of prostitution under the police power. This concerns regulation of bawdy houses, not boarding/lodging houses -- a different vice-regulation doctrine, not our target practice.

cite: Nafe v. Hudson, 19 Tex. Civ. App. 381
notes: Trespass quare clausum fregit over cattle grazing on land held by a tenant at will; farmland possession dispute, no dwelling/lodging letting issue.

cite: Waters-Pierce Oil Co. v. State, 19 Tex. Civ. App. 1
notes: Antitrust forfeiture-of-corporate-permit case against an oil company; discusses police power generally but has no connection to lodging, boarding, or dwelling letting.

cite: Davis v. Washington, 18 Tex. Civ. App. 67
notes: Landlord's-lien dispute over saloon bar fixtures owned by third parties, not the tenant; commercial saloon premises, no lodging/boarding-house issue.

cite: Constantine v. Fresche, 17 Tex. Civ. App. 444
notes: Landlord sued for rent of beach lots and sought a lien on hotel furniture; petition failed to allege any building was leased, so no lien attached. Tenant appears to have run a hotel, but the opinion adjudicates only pleading sufficiency for the lien statute, not the legal character of hotel/lodging operation. No usable characterization holding.

cite: Chambers v. Gilbert, 17 Tex. Civ. App. 106
notes: Police-power condemnation and destruction of glandered livestock; general police-power reasoning but no connection to lodging/dwelling letting. Selector false hit on generic due-process/police-power language.

cite: Oriental Investment Co. v. Sline, 17 Tex. Civ. App. 692
notes: Personal-injury suit by a hotel chambermaid against hotel landlord/operator for an elevator accident (fellow-servant and premises-liability issues). Although set at a hotel, the case addresses employer tort liability, not the legal character or regulation of letting rooms/lodging to guests.

cite: Specht v. Bookhout, 14 Tex. Civ. App. 443
notes: Insolvent corporation's assignment of rents from a leased grain elevator (industrial facility, not a dwelling); receivership/preference-of-creditors dispute, no lodging issue.
